content:
incident-bot: ALERT: deploy-service/canary-health degraded > threshold for 3m — error rate 6% on canary pool (eu-west)
carla_oncall: seeing the same in grafana, canary at 5% of traffic, latency +120ms p95 for model endpoints
alice_sre: tagging this high-priority. carla, are users impacted or only internal probes?
carla_oncall: customer-facing — support reports a few session failures, can confirm increased 5xxs from EU region. escalating to paging.
incident-bot: Pager: carla_oncall (on-call) @channel, recommended runbook: "Canary rollback - immediate"
ben_platform: deployed v2026.4 -> canary slice. initial rollout at 5% traffic. change in KV cache behavior looks suspect from logs.
dmitry_eng: I pulled canary logs, got repeated `KVCacheMissException` + OOM-ish GC spikes on a few replicas. suspicious memory regression in PR #2483.
eve_support: customer-impact: 8 tickets in last 10m, two customers reporting app timeouts. CS triage asked us to notify AE for customers with SLAs. frank_pm: logging impact, will notify priority customers after we have rollback ETA.
carla_oncall: plan proposal: 1) trigger immediate feature-flag kill-switch to stop routing to canary, 2) if traffic doesn't drain in 90s, run manual revert to previous model variant, 3) validate smoke probes, 4) confirm with support then close. objections?
alice_sre: agree. I'll flip flag and run drain. executing now: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/flags/flip -d '{"flag":"canary-routing","state":"off"}'`
alice_sre: flag flipped. routing change acknowledged by control plane. monitoring drain.
carla_oncall: dashboard shows canary traffic to 0.8% now. still seeing some error spikes from lingering pods.
ben_platform: kicking an additional step: scale down canary ASG by 1 to remove problematic replica while drain finishes. executing: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name canary-eu --desired-capacity 2`
ben_platform: scale command accepted.
dmitry_eng: starting quick revert job as safety net (will only run if canary doesn't drop below 0.2% by +120s). command: `deployctl rollback --service deploy-service --to-tag v2026.3 --confirm`
carla_oncall: canary at 0.2% now. errors dropping to baseline. looks like kill-switch did it. hold on verification steps.
dmitry_eng: aborting rollback job since drain succeeded.
alice_sre: running smoke tests against EU canary routing path: `scripts/smoke/eu.sh` -> all checks PASSED (latency within SLO, 200 OK rate 99.98%)
carla_oncall: perf dashboards stable. SLOs recovered.
eve_support: telling CS to pause customer escalations; I'll send an update to affected accounts that we've mitigated and are investigating root cause. frank_pm: will draft post-mortem blurb for customers and execs.
carla_oncall: post-incident next steps: 1) postmortem owner: dmitry_eng, 2) revert PR #2483 until memory regression fixed, 3) add guard in rollout pipeline to run mem usage smoke before canary, 4) formalize kill-switch timing in runbook (drain thresholds).
dmitry_eng: ack. I'll open a rollback PR and start root-cause debugging.
alice_sre: notes for runbook: when flipping flag, verify `routing.percent(canary)` metric hits <0.5% within 90s, otherwise escalate to manual rollback. add exact commands we used here.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: canary routing suppressed, error rate returned to normal, incident closed by carla_oncall.
carla_oncall: closing thread. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
